response: The clinical presentation of a prior preterm birth can predict risk in a subsequent pregnancy. Patients with a history of a prior preterm birth are at an increased risk of having recurrent preterm birth. However, the level of risk may vary depending on the underlying cause of the prior preterm birth. For example, women with a history of cervical shortening or asymptomatic cervical dilation (ACD) are at a higher risk of recurrent preterm birth and cervical shortening in a subsequent pregnancy compared to those with prior preterm birth associated with preterm premature rupture of membranes (PPROM) or preterm labor (PTL). Therefore, the clinical presentation of a prior preterm birth can provide valuable information for predicting risk in a subsequent pregnancy and guiding management decisions.
